subject: Follow-up: BAA availability, PHI boundaries & eligible hosting paths — CareAtlas
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nkh@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wu <emma.wu@careatlas.com>, Tim Holt <tim.holt@careatlas.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: BAA availability, PHI boundaries & eligible hosting paths — CareAtlas

Hi Emma / Tim —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the security & hosting track: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary ask: Can Redwood sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and what hosting modes are eligible for PHI-bearing workloads?
- Secondary: SOC 2 evidence pack and answers to your vendor security questionnaire.
- Constraint: CareAtlas wants clear boundaries where PHI may touch Redwood infrastructure (e.g., inference payloads, logs, backups).

Current position from our side: 
- BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments. These models provide contractual isolation and options for customer-managed keys and audit logging. 
- Hosted API: For our public hosted tier we typically do not sign BAAs by default; in limited cases (short-term pilot with strict controls) we evaluate case-by-case. For production PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- PHI handling boundaries: Our recommended pattern is: client sends inference payloads -> runtime can be configured to avoid retaining request/response payloads in persistent logs, enable KV-cache scrubbing, and use customer-managed KMS for key isolation. Backups and long-term logs are excluded from PHI scope under Dedicated/Private when configured with our compliance options.
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in Q1 2025; Type II assessment is underway with expected completion in Aug 2025. We can share interim evidence and controls mapping now.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I attached our standard vendor security questionnaire and a BAA template. Please complete the questionnaire where helpful and return — we can pre-fill fields on our end too. (attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf, redwood_baa_template.pdf)
2) Marissa (cc'd) — can you lead the SOC2 evidence pull and prepare a short controls summary (logs, access, encryption, incident response) we can share with CareAtlas? Target: 48 hrs.
3) Emma / Tim — confirm whether you prefer Dedicated or Private for the pilot and whether the Hosted path should be evaluated for low-PHI metadata-only calls.

If helpful we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Marissa + your security team to walk the controls and BAA redlines.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nkh@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 12 pages), redwood_baa_template.pdf (DOCX, 8 pages)
From: Emma Wu <emma.wu@careatlas.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nkh@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: BAA availability, PHI boundaries & eligible hosting paths — CareAtlas

Thanks Nikhil — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we start filling the questionnaire: 

- Our default is production PHI must be off-hosted public tiers. We expect BAA-backed deployment (Dedicated or Private) for any PHI in production. Is there a clear differences doc you can share that spells out the exact controls that make Dedicated compliant vs Hosted?
- For data flow: we need to confirm whether any tokenization, telemetry, or error-traceback could contain PHI outside the tenant boundary. Can your SOC2 evidence pack address telemetry/log retention settings and whether those can be turned off or routed to customer-owned logging in Dedicated?
- We'd like to initiate the vendor security questionnaire now — Emma will start and Tim will review. Can Marissa join a 30-min call tomorrow (Tue) at 10:30am PT to go over the controls and expected evidence (SOC sections + specific endpoints for logs)?

Also please send the redwood_baa_template to our legal team (cc'ing them once we have it in DocuSign-ready form).

Best,
Emma
Emma Wu
Head of Security, CareAtlas
emma.wu@careatlas.com

On Mon, Jul 14, 2025 at 09:18 AM Nikhil Sharma <nkh@redwood.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Follow-up: BAA availability, PHI boundaries & eligible hosting paths — CareAtlas

Emma — thanks. Quick reply and actions: 

- Dedicated vs Hosted controls doc: attaching a short "deployment-differences" excerpt in the SOC2 evidence summary (soc2_evidence_summary.pdf). It highlights logging, backup retention, and KMS patterns that differ between tiers.
- Telemetry/log retention: for Dedicated/Private we support routing all runtime logs to your customer-managed logging endpoint (supporting S3/gcs/siem endpoints) and can disable application-level debug traces. The SOC2 evidence summary lists where these controls map to Trust Services Criteria.
- Marissa is available and happy to run the 30-min session tomorrow at 10:30am PT. I'll send a calendar invite after this mail.
- Legal / BAA: I uploaded the BAA template to a shared folder and also attached the DOC here (redwood_baa_template.pdf). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/baatemplate-CareAtlas — please have your legal team review and I'll coordinate DocuSign once we have redlines.

Next steps I will take now:
- Marissa: prepare evidence pack + deployment differences excerpt (ETA: 24-48 hrs).
- I will send calendar invite for Tue 10:30am PT.

Regards,
Nikhil

Attachments: soc2_evidence_summary.pdf, redwood_baa_template.pdf
From: Nikhil Sharma <nkh@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: BAA availability, PHI boundaries & eligible hosting paths — CareAtlas

Marissa — forwarding CareAtlas thread. Ask: can you compile the following into a single packet we can share tomorrow before the call?

1) SOC2 interim evidence list (controls mapping for logging, backups, access controls, incident response)
2) Short one-page differences doc: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (focus: where PHI may be stored/retained and what can be customer-controlled)
3) Any sample audit logs or sanitized samples we can provide (where possible) and a note on retention defaults + how to switch to customer-managed logging

Possible redlines I expect from legal: data flow definitions in the BAA, indemnity carve-outs, and retention clauses. If you can flag which clauses we typically accept vs. escalate to legal, that will speed turnaround.

I will also create the calendar invite for Tue 10:30am PT and include your security alias.

Thanks — feel free to drop your ETA in reply.

Nikhil
